title: Treasury yields are broadly flat as investors await retail sales data
html:
U.S. Treasury yields were little changed on Tuesday morning as investors awaited economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials later in the session.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was broadly flat at 5.118%, while the long-dated 30-year Treasury bond was up just above the flatline to 5.472%. Meanwhile, the 2-year Treasury note yield was down 2 basis points to 4.806%.

One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.

October's retail sales data is due later on Tuesday morning, with economists forecasting retail sales to grow 0.6% on the month, down from 0.8% in September. A stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce the case for higher Fed interest rates.

Investors will also parse comments from the Fed's Alberto Musalem, Christopher Waller and John Williams, who are all due to speak publicly at separate engagements on Tuesday.

The latest FOMC meeting minutes are due on Wednesday, with investors watching for insights on the Fed's October decision to leave interest rates unchanged. Traders are currently pricing in a 95% chance of a quarter-percentage-point hike in December, per the CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Elsewhere in the market, a selloff in key technology and AI stocks continued on Monday amid growing calls to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO. A source familiar with the matter told CNBC on Monday that Nvidia's board of directors is not discussing bringing back the founder.

Additionally, the Commerce Department on Monday moved to close a loophole that let Chinese firms lease Nvidia's computing power from locations in other countries.

Also on the schedule are the weekly initial jobless claims on Thursday and the preliminary Michigan consumer sentiment on Friday.
summary: U.S. Treasury yields were little changed on Tuesday morning as investors awaited economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials later in the session.
